draft.title: Landscapes and landforms
card: A large area of the Earth's surface with its own look. A desert, a coastline or a rainforest is a landscape.
A single natural feature of the land, such as a mountain, valley, dune or headland.
A landscape is made up of many landforms. A coastal landscape may include headlands, beaches and cliffs.
Think of size. A landform is one feature. A landscape is the whole area where many features sit together.
draft.remember: One feature is a landform. Many landforms together make a landscape.

a.q: Which one of these is a landform, not a landscape?
a.why: A dune is one single feature of the land, so it is a landform. A desert, a coastline and a rainforest are each whole areas made of many features, so they are landscapes.
a.clue: Which one is a single feature, not a whole area?

b.q: A walker in the Grampians (Gariwerd) in Victoria crosses high peaks, deep valleys and rocky ridges. What is the whole area best called?
b.why: The area is large and holds many features, so it is a landscape, and its features are mountain ones. Calling it a landform is wrong, because each peak, valley or ridge is a landform, not the whole area.
b.clue: Is the question about the whole area or one feature in it?
